rationale: The v2.6.0 deprecation entry that shipped in the published spec is deleted rather than superseded, and search.dto.ts:46-47 still carries it, so the two rating histories now disagree; a real but small documentation-history concern.
The v3 entry is accurate (0 was coerced to null before 99281de and is rejected now); the cluster mostly clears itself, and the residual 'does not mention -1' point is g01's substance.
Untouched code, phrased as 'worth confirming' with no asserted defect; the existing controller spec already exercises the lat/long refinement through the extended UpdateAssetDto.
A considered-and-cleared note asserting no defect.
Observation about diff rendering of generated files; no defect claimed.

Verified: rating starts at 0 and only >0 propagates, so a -1 on a merged duplicate never carries to an unrated keeper; whether rejection should propagate is debatable, so small and pre-existing rather than substantive.
Verified: -1 is cast to Rating and rendered as no stars, so web cannot distinguish rejected from unrated; real UX gap but pre-existing and outside this server-only change.
Considered-and-cleared note; the Dart model does a bare int.parse with no bounds check, so nothing to act on.

Rating 0 already returned 400 at the checkpoint base (99281de introduced .min(1)); this PR merely relabels the v3 history entry to say so, so it is neither a new breaking change nor undocumented — only the 'no test pins 0' remark is a minor true nit.
Probed and cleared for the tested case; the 1e21 double-issue observation has no practical impact and is not worth reviewer attention.
Commit-message typos on a squash-merged PR are not a code concern.
Purely stylistic preference about the refine error text; the message is accurate.
The deleted migration (merged in 99281de on main) irreversibly nulled -1 ratings wherever it ran; nothing can restore them, but a release-note acknowledgment is a reasonable, small ask.

Verified: BaseSearchSchema.rating still has .min(1) and the '-1 no longer valid' history, so every search DTO rejects rating -1 with 400 while the update DTO now accepts it — rejected assets can be set but not searched, and the two histories contradict.

options[0] is the 'null' entry so options[rating] for 1-5 is correctly indexed (not off by one), and Number.parseInt('null') yields NaN which JSON-serializes to null; pre-existing and unrelated to the diff besides.

Moving bounds into .refine() removes them from the JSON-schema output, so the spec publishes minimum/maximum ±9007199254740991 for UpdateAssetDto/AssetBulkUpdateDto.rating — the same wrong/misleading bounds thread 1 flags.
Verified: the as-is loop still covers only 1 and 5, and the -1 e2e/metadata tests removed by 99281de are not restored, so the PR's headline behavior has no test and a re-restriction would pass CI.
Identical error strings for 7 and -2 are inherent to a single refine predicate; the tests still assert 400 with the right message, so nothing actionable.
Descriptions now diverge (asset.dto.ts mentions -1/rejected; search.dto.ts:41 and exif.dto.ts:32 do not) and the 'rejected' concept is otherwise undocumented; correct but small.
Considered-and-cleared note asserting no defect.

Verified: extraction still uses validateRange(exifTags.Rating, 1, 5), and sidecar write (metadata.service.ts:509,523) emits Rating -1, so a rejection set via the API or authored as XMP is nulled on the next extraction — the -1 change is undone by the metadata path.

Kysely 0.28's Migrator calls ensureNoMissingMigrations unconditionally (verified in upstream source) and throws 'corrupted migrations: previously executed migration ... is missing', so any database that recorded the deleted migration fails runMigrations at startup; a no-op up() would avoid it.

Verified: ExifResponseDto.rating keeps z.int().min(1).max(5) (published as minimum 1 in the spec) while responses may now carry -1; not runtime-enforced since no ZodSerializerDto is applied, but the response contract is now wrong.
Probed and cleared; the chain handles undefined and null the same as the old .nullish().
A -1 rating is genuine EXIF data, so counting it as truthy in the tie-break is not a defect; pre-existing heuristic with no clear action.
Scenario checked and dissolved; no defect asserted.
Considered-and-cleared note; widening request bounds is non-breaking.
States that an untouched file is untouched; no defect.
